why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1–5 require the exact output plus one trailing "\n", which matches "prints exactly … followed by a newline". Check 1 also requires exit=0, as its line says. Check 5's note about the backslash-t JSON escape only makes the expected output precise. It is not an extra rule. Check 6 requires exit=0 and a test that "runs bin/csv2json.js with the --tsv argument on input that contains tab characters and asserts on its output". Failing a test that "only calls parse() directly" follows from "runs bin/csv2json.js". Check 7 requires the flag to be mentioned and an example invocation to be present. That is no stricter than "documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation". The stricter items (another argument position, scope beyond the issue, existing tests still present) are all under "Advisory". No PASS or FAIL condition contains a mutation test, a branch or file-scope rule, or a demand for exact wording.
